points.what: EMEA orders fell 16.1% to 172, a contribution of -33 orders, or 122.2% of the total weekly change.
points.so_what: EMEA alone more than accounts for the overall decline of 27 orders, with other regions netting out against it.

points.what: Search, at 66.6% of orders, fell 8.3% to 627, contributing -57 orders, or 211.1% of the total change.
points.so_what: The week's order decline sits almost entirely in the largest traffic source, so total orders track Search closely.

points.what: Email orders rose 46.3% to 60 (+19 orders) and APAC rose 5.9% to 429 (+24 orders), partly offsetting the declines.
points.so_what: These gains cushioned the week, holding the total order decline to 2.8% rather than a steeper fall.

points.what: AOV was $84.72, down 5.8% week on week and down 3.7% year on year, both assessed as bad.
points.so_what: Lower value per order explains why revenue fell 8.7% while orders fell only 2.8%.

points.what: The cancellation rate was 15.3%, up 0.3 pp on the prior week (bad) but 1.5 pp below last year (good).
points.so_what: Each percentage point of cancellations is worth about $798 of weekly revenue, so the weekly move is small in money terms.

points.what: The 14-Day Return Rate for the mature week of 18 May 2026 was 11.4%, up 0.5 pp week on week and 0.8 pp year on year, both bad.
points.so_what: Returns are running above last year, which matters because gross revenue does not subtract returns.

points.what: New customer signups were 236, down 5.6% week on week and down 6.3% year on year, both assessed as bad.
points.so_what: Customer acquisition is shrinking against last year while orders grew 70.3%, so growth is leaning on existing customers.
